messages:
Mira (product): FYI - three enterprise pilots requested an "evidence assurance" SLA for audit artifacts before we flip the Dedicated toggle. They want: immutable exports, verifiable signatures over time, tenant-level retention lanes, and a clear escrow/rotation option. Can we draft a minimal launch checklist?
Jon (eng-platform): Quick take: we should aim for an append-only export model + RFC3161 timestamping + signed manifest. Practical flow: snapshot -> produce export tar -> compute per-file sha256 -> build manifest -> sign manifest with AsymmetricSign -> optionally timestamp with RFC3161 TSA. That gives non-repudiation without handing over keys.
Adele (security): Strong yes on timestamping. Also want hardware-backed attestations for any Redwood-held signing keys (HSM/PKCS#11). For BYOK we accept tenant-managed AsymmetricSign or uploaded public keys (PEM). Rotation policy: manifest must include signer_id and key_version and we must preserve historical public key records for verification.
Sam (ops): Two operational asks: 1) retrieval latency tiers (hot: sub-5s, warm: <30s, cold: 24-72h), and 2) export generation SLA & throttles. Exports are CPU+io heavy; we should default to "queued within 8h" and offer paid rush lanes. Also legal-hold should toggle retention/purge jobs.
Mira (product): MVP checklist suggestion: a) signed manifest (verifiable by tenant), b) RFC3161 timestamping option, c) retention lanes w/ opt-in long-term cold, d) BYOK + Redwood-HSM signing fallback with attestation, e) legal-hold and purge protection, f) proof-of-delivery audit event + signed receipt. Thoughts?
Jon (eng-platform): Implementation notes: - manifest fields: format, files[], merkle_root (optional), signer_id, key_version, signature (base64), rfc3161_token (optional). Example manifest snippet:
```
format: tar.gz
files:
 - path: audit/2026-03-01.log
   sha256: abcd...
merkle_root: ef01...
signer: projects/redwood-kms/keys/tenant-sign/versions/5
signature: BASE64...
rfc3161_token: BASE64_TSA...
```
We can support merkle tree later, but manifest+timestamp+signature covers most needs.
Adele (security): Add to policy: verification UX must allow customers to upload their current and archived public keys to Console and run a verification check (signature + timestamp + hash checks). Also include tamper detection (e.g., manifest vs file checksums).
Sam (ops): Cost appendix for PRD: hot index ~ $0.025/GB/mo, warm ~ $0.007/GB/mo, cold archive ~ $0.0009/GB/mo. Egress and CPU for export: bill per-export with a small fixed fee + GB egress. We'll produce numbers.
contracts-bot: Legal flag: Please include SLA language for "evidence availability" and a clause for legal-hold overrides. Recommend 30-day evidence delivery warranty for pilot. Tagging @contracts to draft language.
Mira (product): Prioritization/handoff: MVP = signed manifest + timestamping + retention lanes + legal-hold + basic BYOK integration. Stretch: HSM attestation UI, merkle partial proofs, signed receipts ledger.
Jon (eng-platform): Dev estimate: 2 sprints for export plumbing + signing + timestamping, 1 sprint for retention/control-plane + API, 1 sprint for Console verification UI.
Adele (security): I'll draft the rotation/escrow options: (1) tenant-managed KMS (recommended), (2) customer-uploaded public keys with retention of archived keys, (3) third-party escrow process. Include threat model for key compromise and recommended mitigations (revocation list, signed key history).
Sam (ops): I'll draft runbook: export request -> identity check -> enqueue -> snapshot -> sign & timestamp -> stage in S3 -> generate signed receipt -> notify tenant. Include rate limits and size caps.
Mira (product): Action items: Jon - prototype manifest schema + sample CLI by EOD Wed; Adele - rotation/escrow policy + verification checklist; Sam - cost appendix + ops runbook; contracts - SLA appendix. I'll collate into a short PRD and schedule a 30m decision sync.
Jon (eng-platform): Will post a tiny CLI demo: `rwctl export create --tenant t-123 --since 2026-01-01 --sign=rsa-pkcs1 --timestamp=rfc3161`
Adele (security): Verification steps we'll publish: 1) fetch manifest, 2) verify signature w/ key_version, 3) verify RFC3161 token timestamp against manifest hash, 4) spot-check per-file sha256, 5) optionally verify merkle proof if available.
Sam (ops): Also adding a "redaction opt" note - some customers want PII redaction before export. That needs policy review and UI opt-in.
Mira (product): Good catch on redaction. We'll add a separate story for DLP/redaction with legal approvals. Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll run the sync invite.
